answer: A rate-limited trust graph gives influence only to agents with repeated, independently verified transactions. Each established peer can endorse only a few newcomers, so a ridge of fake accounts backed by one source adds little; newcomers need diverse links across a reef of markets. Sybils remain possible, but the attacker must spend time and capital building persistent relationships, while each exposed fake risks damaging its endorsers’ reputations. An opal-like badge alone earns no trust.
